newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam chairs meeting to discuss U.S. attack.
newsitem.headline: Saddam chairs meeting to discuss U.S. attack.

text.p: Iraqi President Saddam Hussein chaired a meeting on Tuesday of Iraq's ruling body to discuss "details of the unjust U.S. aggression" and had taken a number of decisions in response to the missile attack.

The Iraqi news agency INA quoted a spokesman for the meeting of the Revolution Command Council and senior ruling Baath party members as saying Baghdad would also evaluate the position taken by other nations towards the U.S. missile attack on Tuesday on Iraq. He did not elaborate.
"The meeting has taken a number of necessary decisions and measures to face the situation after the cowardly American aggression," said the spokesman.

The spokesman strongly criticised the United States for freezing the implementaion of an oil-for-food deal agreed with the United Nations on May 20 allowing limited amounts of Iraqi oil onto world markets for the first time in six years.
"The U.S. is behaving as if it is the decision-maker in the U.N. Security Council and it is the one who launches aggression under the council's resolutions," he said.
U.S. defence officials said 27 cruise missiles were fired earlier on Tuesday at about 15 targets in southern Iraq including air defence radars, missile sites and command and communication centres.

The United States was prompted into launching the attack by Iraq's military incursion over the weekend into its Kurdish north, where Western allies operate a "no-fly zone" to protect the minority from Baghdad.
